scopePolicy.globalUniverse: Track the broader terpene/terpenoid universe separately from Cannabis occurrence.
scopePolicy.cannabisSet: A compound is marked cannabis-reported only when a traceable analytical or review source supports occurrence in Cannabis.
scopePolicy.cultivarProfiles: Do not assign fixed percentages to a strain name. Percentages belong to individual measured samples or source-reported ranges with provenance.
scopePolicy.stereochemistry: Preserve stereoisomers and isomer ambiguity when the source distinguishes them.
scopePolicy.effects: Do not convert preclinical mechanism data into human treatment claims.

Reported from Cannabis volatile oil in the historical literature summarized by Radwan et al. Formula and identifier are linked to the generic α-thujene PubChem record; specific enantiomeric composition in Cannabis is not asserted here.
Reported among oxygenated Cannabis monoterpenes in the review inventory. PubChem identifier shown for (+)-pulegone; the Cannabis occurrence record does not infer an enantiomer ratio.
Reported from Cannabis essential-oil studies summarized by Radwan et al.; chemistry identifier is from PubChem.

Reported from fresh and stored Cannabis bud volatile-oil work summarized by Radwan et al. PubChem record is the resolved (S)-ipsdienol entry; the review occurrence is retained without asserting Cannabis stereochemical purity.
Reported as a Cannabis sesquiterpene in the historical essential-oil literature summarized by Radwan et al. PubChem identifier is for (+)-longifolene.
Reported from Cannabis essential oil in the review inventory. PubChem entry corresponds to cis-calamenene.

Reported from Cannabis resin in the historical literature summarized by Radwan et al. PubChem contains separate (+) and (−) α-gurjunene records; the Atlas does not assign a single stereoisomer to the Cannabis occurrence without source-specific stereochemical evidence.
Reported among Cannabis sesquiterpenes in the review inventory. PubChem provides the formula, identifier, and a delicate floral odor description.
Reported in Cannabis volatile-oil studies summarized by Radwan et al. PubChem identifier corresponds to the commonly indexed β-elemene stereoisomer.

coverage.target: Expand toward the full literature-backed Cannabis terpene/terpenoid inventory while preserving compound-level provenance and isomer distinctions.
coverage.literatureContext: Recent reviews describe more than 100 Cannabis terpenes, with one synthesis enumerating 61 monoterpenes and 51 sesquiterpenes; coverage varies by analytical method, plant material, and inclusion criteria.
